chunks: Hadith 4459 — Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who instructed another man to marry him to a woman from the people of Basra, from Banu Tamim, but he married him instead to a woman from the people of Kufa, from Banu Tamim.
He عليه السلام said: “He has gone against his command, and upon the one commanded is half of the dowry for the woman’s family. There is no 'iddah upon her, and there is no inheritance between them.”

Then some of those present with him said: “What if he instructed him to marry him to a woman, without naming a land or a tribe, and then the one giving the instruction denied that he had instructed him to do that after he had married him?”

He عليه السلام said: “If the one commanded has proof that he had instructed him to marry him to a wife, then the dowry is upon the one giving the instruction. But if he has no proof, then the dowry is upon the one commanded for the woman’s family. There is no inheritance between them, and there is no 'iddah upon her. She has half of the dowry if he had fixed a dowry for her, and if he had not named a dowry for her, then there is nothing for her.”

key_terms.الصَّدَاقِ: the dowry due in the marriage context
key_terms.الْمَأْمُورِ: the one instructed or appointed to act
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: legal proof or evidence establishing the claim
key_terms.عِدَّةَ: the waiting period ordinarily observed after separation
key_terms.يُزَوِّجَهُ: to arrange a marriage for him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a marriage agent acts against instructions or the one who appointed him later denies authorizing the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on unauthorized or disputed marriage agency. It explains the consequences when an agent acts against instructions or when the principal later denies having authorized the marriage, clarifying liability for the dowry, and ruling out inheritance and 'iddah in such a case.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4459 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Ubaydah, who reported from Abu Abdullah (as):

Regarding a man who instructed another man to marry him to a woman from the people of Basra, from the tribe of Banu Tamim, but the intermediary instead married him to a woman from the people of Kufa, also from the tribe of Banu Tamim.

Imam (as) said: "He has disobeyed his command. The intermediary is responsible for half the dowry to the woman's family. There is no waiting period ('iddah) for her, and there is no inheritance between them."

Someone present then asked: "What if he instructed him to marry a woman without specifying the land or tribe, and later the man who gave the order denied ever instructing him after the marriage had been performed?"

Imam (as) said: "If the intermediary has proof that he was instructed to arrange the marriage, then the dowry is the responsibility of the one who gave the order. However, if the intermediary has no proof, then the dowry falls upon the intermediary to pay to the woman's family. There is no inheritance between them, and there is no waiting period ('iddah) for her. She is entitled to half the dowry if a specific dowry was stipulated. If no dowry was specified, then she is entitled to nothing."
